Lake Powell Hits Record Low Amid Colorado River Water Crisis

Lake Powell, the second-largest reservoir in the US, has reached a record low water level. This event underscores a deepening water crisis affecting the Colorado River, which supplies water and electricity to millions across seven states in the Southwest. The shrinking river levels also pose a threat to hydropower generation, with Lake Powell reportedly 30 feet from a shutdown. The situation highlights the critical state of major reservoirs in the region.
